message.content:
To find out your current internet speed, you can use one of the following methods:

### 1. Online Speed Test Websites  
These sites run a quick test and display your download and upload speeds.

| Website | How to Use |
|---------|------------|
| **Speedtest.net** (by Ookla) | Visit https://www.speedtest.net/, click “Go,” and wait for the results. |
| **Fast.com** (by Netflix) | Go to https://fast.com/; the test starts automatically and shows your download speed. |
| **Google Speed Test** | Search “internet speed test” on Google, and click the “Run Speed Test” button that appears in the search results. |

### 2. Command‑Line Tools  

#### On Windows  
1. Install **speedtest-cli** via PowerShell:
   ```powershell
   pip install speedtest-cli
   ```
2. Run the test:
   ```powershell
   speedtest
   ```

#### On macOS/Linux  
1. Install **speedtest-cli** (requires Python):
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install speedtest-cli   # Debian/Ubuntu
   brew install speedtest-cli           # macOS with Homebrew
   ```
2. Execute:
   ```bash
   speedtest
   ```

### 3. Router’s Built‑In Diagnostics  
Many home routers have a diagnostics page that includes a speed test. Log into your router’s admin interface (usually at http://192.168.0.1 or http://192.168.1.1), navigate to the diagnostics section, and look for a “Speed Test” option.

---

**Tip:** Perform the test several times at different times of day to get an average speed, as bandwidth can fluctuate based on network traffic.
